source.title: The Linear Geometry of Interpretable Tokens: Jailbreaking Attacks and Defenses for Unlearned Diffusion Models
source.authors: Si-Yi Chen; Yimeng Zhang; Sijia Liu; Qing Qu

record.tranche_reason: The study finds an attack-accessible residual that is usefully represented by a subspace of multiple orthogonal token-embedding directions, refining a single-direction account. It does not test sparse-feature superposition under dimensional capacity pressure.
record.gate_note: The paper studies residual representations in unlearned diffusion models, not toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions. Its K-prefix attack results bear on whether the attack-accessible residual is captured by one direction or several. Other attack and defense performance results are not rows because they do not measure the dimensionality claim.
record.test_reason: The paper studies jailbreak attacks and defenses for unlearned Stable Diffusion v1.4 models. It builds attack token embeddings as linear combinations of CLIP token embeddings, drawing on the linear-representation idea, and reports its own method's ASR, transfer and defense results. It does not test superposition in any of its versions. There are no sparse features outnumbering dimensions, no polysemantic neurons, no SAEs, and no test of whether features are 1-D or multi-dimensional. The K-direction results (Table 18) are best-of-K coverage: each attack uses a single direction, and success means any one of K separate directions works. That measures how many distinct single-direction attacks exist, not the dimensionality of a feature. It is the study's own method performance.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a coherent, interpretable, attack-accessible linear residual of the erased concept can be recovered in the token embedding space. They state this does not assert the representation is exclusively linear or that the subspace is unique, and that both SubAttack and SubDefense follow from this structure.
record.recipe_differences: This is a diffusion-model token-embedding attack and defense, not a sparse-feature toy-network superposition experiment. It learns orthogonal attack directions by deflation and evaluates attack coverage as the number of directions increases.
record.method_sensitivity: Attack coverage increases as the number of included directions increases in the reported ESD–nudity prefix evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: An erased concept in unlearned diffusion models stays reachable through many orthogonal token-embedding directions. Best-of-K attack coverage rises from 61.7% (K=1) to 88.7% (K=30) against a 15.0% baseline. Rank-100 bases from independent runs overlap at about 0.31, versus 0.13 for random subspaces.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual concept information after diffusion unlearning is accessible through a reproducible, multi-direction linear subspace of the text-encoder token embedding space.

record.problems: The dimensionality evidence is from one ESD–nudity protocol with 60 examples; the paper states that evaluation primarily studies Stable Diffusion v1.4 with a CLIP text encoder. The learned attack directions are not shown to be complete or canonical representation units.
record.rows_left_out: Attack-success and defense results in the main tables and appendices were not extracted because they do not specifically measure the dimensionality of the attack-accessible residual.

untested.parts: Not tested: no toy networks, no sparsity-dependent transition, no feature geometry under capacity pressure.
Not tested: no neurons or capacity competition.
Not tested: no LLMs and no SAE recovery.
Not tested: no SAE features. The authors explicitly do not claim the recovered subspace is unique or complete.
Not tested: multiple single directions each trigger the concept, but no test of whether the model's features are 1-D or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the K-direction rows to V6 and labelled them supports. Changed: best-of-K coverage with each direction used separately is a measure of the method's attack performance, not of feature dimensionality. The paper uses no superposition framing, and its linear-representation citations are motivation only. Relation set to uses_without_test, tranche T4.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test feature-over-dimension capacity pressure, sparse co-activity, or the predicted sparsity-dependent geometry in small networks.
No neuron polysemanticity or competition for dedicated versus shared dimensions is tested.
The study does not measure polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
The study concerns diffusion models, not LLM feature distribution or SAE recovery in LLMs.
The study does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.

The study tests the attackable residual's performance as additional learned directions are used, but does not establish that these directions are canonical or exhaustive units of the model's representation.

rows.note: The reported statistic is aggregated across learned runs. Each learned attack token embedding is a direction; this is the one-direction prefix result.
rows.check: Best-of-prefix ASR of the study's own attack. Each candidate is one direction used alone, so the measure cannot show whether a feature is 1-D or multi-dimensional. This is method performance, not a V6 measurement.
